source.subject: Biology
source.unit: Unit 1 — Diversity in the Living World
source.source_scope: Only the content printed on PDF page 3 (printed page 12): how the five kingdom system reclassified fungi, prokaryotes and unicellular eukaryotes, the phylogenetic approach, the start of Section 2.1 Kingdom Monera, bacterial shapes, and Figure 2.1.

questions.question: Fungi were placed in a separate kingdom partly because their cell walls contain, unlike the cellulosic walls of green plants:
questions.explanation: The page contrasts the chitin in fungal walls with the cellulosic cell wall of green plants.
questions.source_text: in their walls while the green plants had a cellulosic cell wall.

questions.question: In the five kingdom system, all prokaryotic organisms are grouped under:
questions.explanation: The page says all prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under Kingdom Monera.
questions.source_text: All prokaryotic organisms were grouped together under Kingdom Monera

questions.question: Which kingdom contains the unicellular eukaryotic organisms?
questions.explanation: The page says the unicellular eukaryotic organisms were placed in Kingdom Protista.
questions.source_text: the unicellular eukaryotic organisms were placed in Kingdom Protista.

questions.question: Which of these organisms are named on the page as brought together in Kingdom Protista?
questions.explanation: Kingdom Protista brought together Chlamydomonas and Chlorella with Paramoecium and Amoeba.
questions.source_text: Kingdom Protista has brought together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella

questions.question: Chlamydomonas and Chlorella were earlier placed under:
questions.explanation: The page says they were earlier placed in algae within Plants and both had cell walls.
questions.source_text: (earlier placed in Algae within Plants and both having cell walls)

questions.question: Paramoecium and Amoeba were earlier placed in:
options: The animal kingdom, which lacks cell walls
questions.explanation: The page says they were earlier placed in the animal kingdom which lacks cell wall.
questions.source_text: (which were earlier placed in the animal kingdom which lack cell wall)

questions.question: Kingdom Protista put together organisms that earlier belonged to different kingdoms. This happened because:
options: Cell walls were found in all of them
Protozoa were discovered to be plants
questions.explanation: The page says this happened because the criteria for classification changed.
questions.source_text: This happened because the criteria for classification changed.

questions.question: A classification that is 'phylogenetic' is based on:
questions.explanation: The page defines phylogenetic as based on evolutionary relationships.
questions.source_text: but is also phylogenetic, i.e., is based on evolutionary relationships.

questions.question: In which chapters are Kingdoms Plantae and Animalia dealt with separately?
questions.explanation: The page says the plant and animal kingdoms will be dealt with separately in chapters 3 and 4.
questions.source_text: will be dealt separately in chapters 3 and 4.

questions.question: Which organisms are the sole members of Kingdom Monera?
questions.explanation: The page states that bacteria are the sole members of Kingdom Monera.
questions.source_text: Bacteria are the sole members of the Kingdom Monera.

questions.question: Which habitats are mentioned where bacteria live, including those where very few other life forms survive?
questions.explanation: The page says bacteria occur almost everywhere, including hot springs, deserts, snow and deep oceans.
questions.source_text: such as hot springs, deserts, snow and deep oceans where very few other life forms can survive.

questions.question: According to the page, bacteria are:
questions.explanation: The page says bacteria are the most abundant micro-organisms and that many live in or on other organisms as parasites.
questions.source_text: They are the most abundant micro-organisms.

questions.question: Into how many categories are bacteria grouped based on their shape on this page?
questions.explanation: Coccus, Bacillus, Vibrium and Spirillum make four shape categories.
questions.source_text: Bacteria are grouped under four categories based on their shape

questions.question: Match each bacterial form with its shape.
questions.explanation: The page gives: spherical Coccus, rod-shaped Bacillus, comma-shaped Vibrium and spiral Spirillum.
questions.source_text: the spherical Coccus (pl.: cocci), the rod-shaped Bacillus (pl.: bacilli), the comma-shaped Vibrium (pl.: vibrio) and the spiral Spirillum (pl.: spirilla)

questions.question: The plural of Spirillum, as given on the page, is:
questions.explanation: The page gives spirilla as the plural of Spirillum.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Kingdom Protista put together organisms that earlier classifications had placed in different kingdoms.
Reason (R): The criteria used for classification had changed.
options: Both A and R are true, and R correctly explains A
Both A and R are true, but R does not explain A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation: The page gives the changed classification criteria as the reason for this regrouping.
questions.source_text: It has put together organisms which, in earlier classifications, were placed in different kingdoms. This happened because the criteria for classification changed.
